input.rationale: Of the three compositions measured, Cu0.56Fe0.12V0.31 gave the highest photocurrent: 1.4e-7 A. That is about 3x the V-rich CuV2O6-like point (#58) and about 5x the Cu3Fe4V6O24-like point (#200). This fits the known photoanode activity of Cu-rich Cu vanadates (Cu3V2O8/Cu2V2O7 type) near the 2.06 eV illumination energy.

content.text:
I submitted index 131 (Cu 0.56, Fe 0.12, V 0.31). It had the highest photocurrent of the three compositions I measured, at 1.4×10⁻⁷ A. With only 3 measurements across 296 candidates, I can't tell how close it is to the best composition in the library.

The merit budget was 3, and I picked each point from what I know about these materials rather than from the data:

| Index | Composition (Cu / Fe / V) | Why I picked it | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|---|
| 200 | 0.24 / 0.30 / 0.46 | Near Cu₃Fe₄(VO₄)₆, a reported quaternary photoanode | 3×10⁻⁸ A |
| 58 | 0.29 / 0.10 / 0.61 | Vanadium-rich, near CuV₂O₆ | 5×10⁻⁸ A |
| 131 | 0.56 / 0.12 / 0.31 | Copper-rich copper vanadate region (Cu₃V₂O₈ / Cu₂V₂O₇ type) | 1.4×10⁻⁷ A |

Two gaps:
- **No XRD measurements:** I didn't use any of the 5, so the phase behind the best result is inferred from composition, not confirmed.
- **Phase list not read:** it was too large to return in full, so I didn't read it.

The large iron-rich part of the library was never measured. So "copper-rich is best" is only a trend across three points, not a map of the library.
